customer_question: We have several product variants that all use the same module and stack -- can they all be registered under the one Host Subsystem DID we're creating?
question_variants: Can multiple of our products share a single Host Subsystem registration ID?
Do we need a separate DID for each product variant using the same module?
How do we cover several same-module product variants without registering each separately?
actual_issue: The customer had several product variants that all used the same module and Bluetooth stack, and wanted to know whether they could all be registered under the single Host Subsystem DID being created for this engagement, rather than requiring separate registrations.
plain_english_explanation: Strictly speaking, a single registration record itself doesn't hold multiple separate products bundled into it -- but that's not really the practical concern. What actually matters is whether several product variants using identical Bluetooth hardware and software can all be covered without paying for and completing a brand-new registration each time, and the answer to that practical question is yes, through a simple free add-on process available once the first registration is done.
consultant_answer: Strictly speaking, a single Host Subsystem DID cannot have multiple products registered into it directly -- registering to the Product List applies to the 'new Host Subsystem + combined Controller Subsystem registration' as a whole, not the Host Subsystem portion alone. However, interpreting the question as asking whether products sharing the same module and stack, with the same Bluetooth functionality, can be added to the new registration's Product List: yes. Once the new registration is complete, it appears in the registrant's Listing Manage page list, with an 'Add Product' link on the far right of that entry. From that link, derivative products can be added to the Product List for free at any time through a simple web operation, and the corresponding procedure documentation is delivered at the completion of the engagement.
decision_logic: While a single Host Subsystem DID does not itself hold multiple registered products directly, the practical goal of covering multiple product variants that share the same module and stack is achieved through the free, self-service 'Add Product' mechanism on the registrant's Listing Manage page, available once the initial registration is complete.
final_recommendation: When a customer asks whether multiple same-module/stack product variants can be covered without registering each separately, clarify that the DID itself doesn't hold multiple products directly, but that the free 'Add Product' self-service mechanism on the Listing Manage page achieves the same practical outcome once the initial registration is complete.
risk_if_done_wrong: Telling a customer that multiple products can be registered directly into one Host Subsystem DID, without clarifying the actual mechanism (the separate, free Product List addition process), could create confusion about how to actually add their product variants.
